title: finding: 4 of the 6 `checkFieldRefs` threading sites in `validate-react-page-props` can drop the `unprovisionedAnchors` index with the whole lint suite staying green
body:
Measured while implementing #8664 (which corrects the `unprovisionedAnchors` parameter comment on `checkFieldRefs`). Filed as an observation; **not fixed** — #8664's scope is the prose claim, and adding these pins is the other half its grading told the implementer not to mix in.

## What was measured

`checkFieldRefs` (`packages/lint/src/validate-page-field-bindings.ts`) takes the anchor index as an OPTIONAL trailing parameter, so a call site that stops passing it keeps compiling and silently downgrades to the pre-#8340 behaviour (existence answered, provenance never asked).

I dropped the argument at each in-repo threading site in turn and ran `packages/lint`'s suite. Result:

| # | Site | Drop the index ⇒ |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | `validate-page-field-bindings.ts:433` — `validatePageFieldBindings` | **RED** — "warns on a highlights binding over an unprovisioned anchor…" |
| R0 | `validate-react-page-props.ts:1100` — `validateReactPageProps` into `checkBlockFieldProps` | **RED** — "reaches the FILTER position through the shared core…" |
| R2 | `validate-react-page-props.ts:849` — `queried` refs | **RED** — same test |
| R1 | `validate-react-page-props.ts:846` — `own` refs (`skipped`) | **GREEN** |
| R3 | `validate-react-page-props.ts:858` — `ObjectForm` subform child refs | **GREEN** |
| R4 | `validate-react-page-props.ts:863` — `subs.parent` (`totalField` rollup) | **GREEN** |
| R5 | `validate-react-page-props.ts:873-880` — the `COMPONENT_FIELD_SPECS` / Block path | **GREEN** |

"GREEN" means the full `@objectstack/lint` suite (73 files, 2045 tests) passes with the index dropped, and typecheck is unaffected — the parameter is optional and the local `unprovisionedAnchors` binding stays read by the sibling call sites, so there is no TS6133 either.

## Why it is worth recording

The two **module seams** are pinned (P1, R0), which is what #8664's corrected comment now states and what #8404 established as the pattern. But four of the react surface's own calls are threaded by convention only. Each is a real author-facing surface: the `skipped` display refs, `ObjectForm` subforms, the `totalField` rollup, and every `COMPONENT_FIELD_SPECS`-driven block. A refactor that reorders or rewrites `checkBlockFieldProps` can quietly drop provenance on any of them, and #8340's warning simply stops appearing for those surfaces — the silent-zero / blank-column failure it exists to announce comes back with every gate green.

This is the same shape as the #8404 pin in `validate-react-page-props.test.ts`, whose comment records exactly this reasoning for the `searchableFields` call ("with the argument dropped here… the whole lint suite stays green. This test is the only thing that goes red"). That claim re-verifies today; these four sites are the calls that have no such pin.

## Suggested disposition

One behaviour test per uncovered site, through `validateReactPageProps`, asserting `page-field-unprovisioned` on an ADR-0015 `external` object — mirroring the existing FILTER-position test. Each should be written ablation-first: drop the argument, watch the new test go red, restore.

Related: #8664, #8340, #8404, #8116.
